Find the median of $4,9,2,11,7,15$.
Find the mode of $3,7,5,7,2,7,9$.
questions.answer: The value 7 appears most often, so the mode is $7$.

questions.q: Find the range of the data set $22,18,35,9,27$.
Find the interquartile range (IQR) of $4,7,9,12,15,18,21$.
questions.answer: Lower half (excluding the median 12): $4,7,9$, so $Q_1=7$. Upper half: $15,18,21$, so $Q_3=18$. IQR $=18-7=11$.

The bar graph shows the results of rolling a fair die 40 times. Based on the experimental data, find the experimental probability of rolling a 4, and compare it to the theoretical probability.
questions.answer: Experimental $P(4)=\dfrac{9}{40}=0.225$. Theoretical $P(4)=\dfrac{1}{6}\approx0.167$. The experimental probability is somewhat higher than the theoretical probability, which is expected random variation in a finite sample.

questions.q: A game costs 2 dollars to play. A player wins 10 dollars with probability 0.1, and wins nothing otherwise. Find the expected net profit per play.
questions.answer: Expected winnings $=0.1\times10=1$ dollar. Expected net profit $=1-2=-1$ dollar (an expected loss of 1 dollar per play).

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a survey of students

questions.q: This question has three parts. A researcher surveys 200 students about whether they play a sport and whether they play a musical instrument. Of the 200 students, 120 play a sport, 80 play an instrument, and 30 do both. (a) Find how many students do neither activity. (b) Find the probability that a randomly chosen student plays a sport or an instrument (or both). (c) Given that a randomly selected student plays a sport, find the probability that they also play an instrument.
questions.answer: (a) By inclusion-exclusion, the number doing at least one activity is $120+80-30=170$. Neither $=200-170=30$. (b) $P(\text{sport or instrument})=\dfrac{170}{200}=0.85$. (c) $P(\text{instrument}\mid\text{sport})=\dfrac{P(\text{both})}{P(\text{sport})}=\dfrac{30}{120}=\dfrac{1}{4}$.
